WattEV opened its eighth California depot at the Port of Oakland in November, following a June opening in Fresno. EV Realty opened a 76-port, 9-megawatt hub in San Bernardino in April, and Prologis added a 32-port hub in Vernon in June. Tesla expanded its network to Hodgkins, Illinois, and Mesquite, Texas, in November. Several projects target 2027. Zeem plans to open its Terminal Island depot at the Port of Long Beach in the first quarter, and Nevoya expects to start a Houston–Dallas operation with 63 Class 8 electric trucks in early 2027. pending_summary: Overhaul, a cargo security company, is urging US shippers to check holiday hours at receiving facilities before loads due between Nov. 23 and Nov. 29 leave origin. The company said trailers staged outside receivers, including big-box stores, are likely targets for pilferage or outright theft, and that the long weekend can give thieves more time before a loss is discovered. It said deception tactics such as double brokering, fraudulent carrier identities and falsified paperwork remain common. Overhaul reported that electronics made up 23.3% of thefts in the third quarter of 2026, a rise of 7.3 percentage points from a year earlier. Recommended steps include GPS tracking, secure parking, vetting brokers and drivers, and avoiding extended staging. Overhaul also said drivers whose photos do not match their CDL, or whose equipment has temporary placards or painted-over logos, should not depart with a load.

The six-hour operation took place on October 28 at the Woodburn northbound and southbound weigh stations, where officers stopped 84 trucks that bypassed the open scale, according to the office's November 22 update. title: 'It helps a lot': Charlotte program trains aspiring truck drivers in face of national shortage, Trump restrictions
orig_title: 'It helps a lot': Charlotte program trains aspiring truck drivers in face of national shortage, Trump restrictions
summary:
A training program run by NCIA in Charlotte currently enrolls about a dozen people in a commercial driver's license course. The Baltimore-based group serves people who face employment barriers, and through a partnership with Transtech CDL Training, enrollees get about four weeks of instruction. People in hardship, such as food stamp recipients and survivors of domestic violence, have their license costs covered, which can otherwise run five to six thousand dollars.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about 214,500 openings a year over the next decade as drivers retire or leave the field. In February, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy issued a rule that makes immigrants ineligible for CDLs when states cannot check their driving records. Duffy said the rule closes a loophole that lets non-citizens obtain CDLs with federal Employment Authorization Documents.

title: Winter Road Conditions Across the Midwest: How Truckers and Dispatchers Check Routes Before Departure
orig_title: Winter Road Conditions Across the Midwest: How Truckers and Dispatchers Check Routes Before Departure
summary:
This Container News guide explains how drivers and dispatchers can check winter road conditions before leaving on trips through Ohio, Indiana and Kentucky. It says snow and freezing rain in Ohio can affect freight headed west hours after a driver has left, so dispatchers should build those changes into routing and scheduling. The article lists OHGO, GoKY, INDOT Traffic Wise, weather alerts and Trucker Guide camera views as tools for checking routes.

The article notes that state crews do not maintain county, township or city roads, so the final miles to a delivery site may not be clear even when the highway is. It also cautions that traffic cameras show only specific spots and do not replace official reports of closures, crashes or restrictions. Dispatchers are advised to keep tracking conditions after departure and to put safety ahead of on-time arrival if a route turns hazardous.

orig_title: Trucker who crashed off Pascagoula River Bridge identified, cause still unknown
summary: A tractor-trailer driver, identified as 64-year-old Norberto Barahona-Mejia of Conroe, Texas, died after his truck left the Pascagoula River Bridge on I-10 in Jackson County, Mississippi, on November 17. According to a report citing WKRG, the crash happened around 12:15 a.m., after the truck collided with a Honda Accord that was also eastbound, and the trailer went over the side of the bridge into the water below. The 27-year-old driver of the Honda Accord and a 28-year-old passenger were injured and are expected to make full recoveries. Officials are still investigating, and the cause has not been released.

title: Bot Auto launches ‘Capacity Grid’ with agreements for 200 million miles of driverless trucking
orig_title: Bot Auto launches ‘Capacity Grid’ with agreements for 200 million miles of driverless trucking
summary:
Bot Auto has launched Capacity Grid, a network intended to match shipper and broker demand with driverless trucking capacity, and has signed agreements covering 200 million miles of driverless freight operations. Customers can reserve capacity for set routes and time windows at agreed prices, buying transportation by the mile without owning trucks. FreightVana, a logistics company specializing in power-only freight transportation, has a commitment covering 50 million miles.

The company said a driverless load ran from northeast Houston to Hutchins, near Dallas, on April 29, covering 231 miles for Ryan Transportation. Figures reported by the company put the driverless trip at $1.89 per mile, against $3.78 for a comparable human-driven operation within its business. Bot Auto has not specified when the full 200 million miles will be completed.

summary: Alberta's government is proposing Bill 43, the Safe and Sensible Roads Act, which would amend the province's Traffic Safety Act to toughen penalties for unsafe trucking. Under the bill, fines for unsafe commercial truck operators would rise from $10,000 to $50,000 for violations including repeated safety breaches and bridge strikes. Driver licences could also be cut to a basic Class 5 licence or made subject to conditions after serious incidents such as a bridge strike. Transportation Minister Devin Dreeshen said retraining would be required before a driver returns to regular duties. If the bill passes, the government would publish information on non-compliant carriers, drivers, driving schools, inspection facilities and company owners and directors. Separately, a Calgary Police Service blitz in September pulled 100 of 197 stopped commercial vehicles off the road for critical defects. In March, a truck hauling equipment struck a rail bridge in Lethbridge, knocking concrete loose and leading to costly repairs for the municipality.

summary:
Two semi drivers died after their trucks collided head-on on Highway 71, north of Lake Minatare Road, outside Scottsbluff, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at about 9:10 a.m., according to authorities. The northbound driver was identified as 66-year-old Wesley Barkell of Pine Bluffs, Wyoming, and the southbound driver as 38-year-old Robert Henderson of Hemingford, Nebraska. The crash happened in foggy conditions. Three other vehicles drove into the scene and were damaged by debris before emergency crews arrived, but their occupants were uninjured.

Highway 71 was shut down in the area for about nine hours. The Nebraska State Patrol is conducting a full crash reconstruction, including post-crash inspections of both commercial vehicles, and no cause for the collision has been released.

title: FMCSA seeks input on using cameras in place of truck mirrors
orig_title: FMCSA seeks input on using cameras in place of truck mirrors
summary: FMCSA has opened a public comment period on a request to let fleets use Safety Vision's View Smart cameras instead of the two side mirrors required on commercial trucks and buses. A notice published Nov. 18 in the Federal Register says Safety Vision is seeking a five-year exemption from the rule requiring a rear-vision mirror on each side, and the agency has not approved the request. The system uses weatherproof cameras on both sides that feed video to screens mounted along the windshield, which the company says offers a wider view, better low-light visibility and alerts for nearby pedestrians or vehicles. Safety Vision has supplied the system to transit bus operators since 2024, though those buses still carry their required mirrors. FMCSA will weigh the application, safety analyses and public comments before deciding whether the system offers safety equal to conventional mirrors. Comments are accepted at Regulations.gov through Dec. 18 under docket FMCSA-2026-3707.

Connecticut State Police are investigating a fatal crash in Tolland that involved a semi truck's brake rotor. Troopers responded to a reported incident on westbound I-84 near Exit 69 around 12:45 p.m. on November 18. Investigators said Juan Marty Del Toro was driving a 2014 Nissan NV200 west when a 2019 Kenworth truck operated by Manpreet Singh was eastbound nearby.

Police said the Kenworth suffered a brake failure that caused rotors to come apart and become airborne. One rotor hit the Nissan, came through the windshield and struck Marty Del Toro, who was pronounced dead at the scene. A passenger was taken to a hospital for evaluation. Police asked anyone with additional information or dash cam video to come forward.

Saia wants commercial learner's permit holders in its driver training program to operate combination vehicles with double trailers while under the direct supervision of a CDL holder with a doubles/triples endorsement. The notice states that it does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach.

Saia has requested a 5-year exemption from two rules, 49 CFR 383.93(b)(1) and 383.37(a). According to the filing, approximately 300 trainees a year would use a fleet of about 19 training vehicles. title: Q3 2026 Cargo Theft Falls as Losses Rise
orig_title: Q3 2026 Cargo Theft Falls as Losses Rise
summary:
Verisk CargoNet reported 547 supply chain crime incidents involving cargo across the U.S. and Canada in the third quarter of 2026, down 33% from a year earlier and 19% from the second quarter. Estimated losses still rose 12% to $230.1 million. Fictitious pickups, in which criminals use deception to obtain a shipment, fell only 6% to 138, so their share of reported activity rose to about 25%.

Through September, reported incidents were down 25% year to date, while estimated losses rose 39% to $718.9 million. The average value of stolen goods with a documented value rose 72% to $448,456. CargoNet logged 19 thefts of $1 million or more, compared with nine a year earlier. California accounted for about a third of incidents, and four states made up 57% of the quarterly total. CargoNet also documented fraud schemes in 2026 that used compromised email accounts, internet phone systems and transportation applications, and said theft has historically risen in Q4.

title: Higher diesel prices strain farm transportation budgets
orig_title: Higher diesel prices strain farm transportation budgets
summary:
Higher diesel prices are adding costs for Iowa farmers and trucking operators, according to Matt Wells, vice president of the Mid-West Truckers Association. Wells cited refinery shutdowns, declining fuel reserves and the war between Russia and Ukraine as factors tightening supply. He said two California refineries were shut down and a refinery in Joliet, Illinois, was offline for seven to ten days, while Ukrainian attacks damaged Russian refining facilities.

Wells said transportation rates and operating budgets will need to reflect the higher costs, potentially for the next year to year and a half, and he does not expect diesel prices to fall significantly soon. He also cautioned that fuel prices do not always return to earlier levels after a large increase. On red-dyed diesel, Wells said the modern dyed product is essentially the same fuel as clear highway diesel, and that its use on public roads remains subject to federal and state tax requirements and any specifically authorized exemptions.

summary:
John Deere is testing 100% biodiesel (B100) in five semi-trucks for six months under its Field to Freight initiative, according to an RFD-TV interview with John Deere Biofuels Director Nate Green. The trucks deliver parts and equipment to dealers and farmers from the company's distribution center in Milan, Illinois, and were fitted with an upgrade kit installed by Optimus Technologies. Penske, CPC Logistics and Chevron are also involved, with Chevron supplying the biodiesel.

The trucks use a dual-tank system to start on diesel and switch to B100 once the engine warms, and they recirculate diesel at shutdown. Green said the demonstration will show whether the technology works within the company's logistics network, and John Deere would consider wider deployment if it does. He also said full life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions from biodiesel can be 50% to 85% lower than petroleum diesel, depending on feedstock.

title: U.S. rail carload and intermodal volume continues strong momentum in October, reports AAR
orig_title: U.S. rail carload and intermodal volume continues strong momentum in October, reports AAR
summary: The Association of American Railroads said U.S. rail carload and intermodal volumes stayed strong in October, according to its latest Rail Industry Overview. The AAR said 15 of its 20 tracked carload commodity groups rose from a year earlier, and 16 were up on a year-to-date basis. Grain, petroleum and petroleum products, chemicals and metallic ores led the year-to-date gains. The report called October intermodal volume "especially strong," citing the first, third and fifth-best intermodal weeks on record, and said 2026 is expected to set a new record. Cited drivers included high diesel prices, trucker insurance and maintenance costs, fewer available truck drivers and solid rail performance.

title: Two men sentenced after CBSA officers stopped an illegal crossing in Manitoba
orig_title: Two men sentenced after CBSA officers stopped an illegal crossing in Manitoba
summary: Two people have been sentenced over an illegal border crossing at the Sprague crossing in Manitoba. The Canada Border Services Agency said it stopped a minivan on May 7 because of "inconsistencies" in the driver's declaration, and officers found a 46-year-old man hiding in the trunk. That man, Temitope Omofuyi Davies, told officers he had paid the driver $1,000 to get him into Canada, and the agency later learned he had also been caught trying to cross near Surrey, B.C., in March. Davies pleaded guilty to failure to report on Aug. 19 and was sentenced to time served. The driver, Annan Nigel Ferguson, a 50-year-old American citizen, was sentenced on Nov. 4 to one year in prison for aiding and abetting failure to report. With time served counted, he has roughly three months left on the sentence.

summary: Bain & Company's 2026 new US Truck Study found that close to 80% of American fleet operators intend to make large equipment investments within six to 12 months. The survey of 210 operators also found that 79% expect fleet growth over the next 12 months, and more than a third of those expect growth of 10% or more. summary: A wrongful death lawsuit has been filed against Contract Transportation Systems Co. (CTS) and one of its truck drivers over a fatal crash on White Horse Road in Greenville, South Carolina. The plaintiff says McPeak suffered severe injuries and died, and accuses the driver of negligence and of violating South Carolina traffic laws and federal motor carrier safety rules. The suit also accuses CTS of negligent hiring, retention, training and supervision, seeks actual, consequential and punitive damages, and has requested a jury trial.

summary: FleetOwner's annual Trucking By the Numbers feature looks at driver figures for for-hire and private fleets. Citing the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, it puts the number of heavy- and tractor-trailer truck drivers at about 2.2 million in 2025. According to the American Transportation Research Institute, the ratio of drivers to trucks dropped to 0.9 that year, and for-hire annual turnover was about 44.2%, down from 48% in 2024. The article says turnover was highest at the largest truckload fleets, at 70.7%. A National Private Truck Council survey of 89 private fleet respondents reported a 17.1% turnover rate, with about 58% of private fleet drivers able to go home every night. Compared with the ATA annualized salary, the surveyed private fleets paid about 19% higher wages.

title: Effort to get trucks off Van Dam in Saratoga Springs continues to stall
orig_title: Effort to get trucks off Van Dam in Saratoga Springs continues to stall
summary:
Saratoga Springs residents and city officials are again pushing to move tractor-trailer traffic off Van Dam Street. The push followed a late-night crash between a Skidmore College bus and a tractor-trailer that blocked traffic for hours at Van Dam and Clinton streets, though no major injuries occurred.

A five-ton weight limit ordinance the City Council passed in December 2023 came down within days, because the state said city officials had no authority to pass local ordinances on the state-designated route. A city request for a traffic study outlined rerouting trucks via Route 9 from Northway exit 14 in Malta or via Route 50 through Ballston Spa. The state said de-designating a route requires documented operational deficiencies or a provable history of accidents. A neighborhood association study counted upward of 700 trucks a day, and the Trucking Association of New York warned that de-designation could push trucks onto other routes.

summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Nov. 5 it will provide $1.5 million to help states improve how they notify vehicle owners about open safety recalls. Funded state programs would develop reliable notification methods tied to vehicle registration and renewal, measure how many recalled vehicles get repaired, and document results so other states can adopt successful practices. NHTSA also wants applicants to study how owners respond to different notification methods and track whether repairs follow. The program is not specifically aimed at commercial trucks, but the article notes that better alerts could help carriers and owner-operators plan repairs. States have until Feb. 4, 2027 to apply, and NHTSA has not said which states will receive grants or when new systems might start. The initiative does not set new commercial maintenance requirements.
